exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, forearms, core
instructions: Set the bell in front of you, hinge and hike it back between the legs like a swing.
Drive the hips and keep the elbow close to the ribs so the bell travels up, not out.
Loosen the grip and slide the hand around the handle so the bell rolls onto the forearm.
Finish in the rack with the wrist straight and forearm vertical, then drop it back into the next hike.
exercises.formCue: Elbow glued to the ribs, bell goes up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Casting the bell away from the body so it bangs the forearm, and gripping too hard to let it roll.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise low swings and a two-hand clean before going to one hand.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A clean rack is the starting point for kettlebell presses, squats and carries.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
instructions: Stand hip width apart with one bell and swing it back between the legs with a flat back.
Drive the hips, pull the bell up close and drop the elbow to the ribs to catch it at the shoulder.
Pause in the rack, then press the bell overhead to a straight arm.
Pull the elbow back down to the rack and let the bell swing back for the next rep.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing from a loose rack and leaning back to finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Split it up: do sets of cleans, then sets of presses.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a hip-driven pull and an overhead press in one repeatable rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, upper back, shoulders, grip
instructions: Hinge with a slight knee bend and swing the bell back until the forearm meets the inner thigh.
Extend the hips and legs hard with the arm still straight.
Shrug and pull the bell close to the body, and near head height punch the hand through the handle.
Finish with the arm locked overhead and the bell resting softly on the forearm, hips and knees straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arm early, letting the bell swing wide, and catching with a bent elbow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Build it from deadlifts, swings and the clean and press before snatching.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It takes a load from low to overhead in one move, building power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand hip width apart with the bell racked at the shoulder, resting on the forearm, elbow near the ribs.
Brace the trunk and squeeze the handle.
Press the arm straight overhead.
Pull the elbow back down to the ribs to return to the rack.
exercises.formCue: Straight wrist, elbow under the bell.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the wrist bend back and leaning away from the bell.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bell, or press from a half-kneeling position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: One-arm pressing builds shoulder strength while the trunk resists the offset load.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
instructions: Hold a light bell upside down by the handle at shoulder height, base pointing at the ceiling.
Stand with the same-side foot slightly forward and crush the handle.
Press the arm straight overhead while keeping the bell balanced.
Pull the elbow back to the ribs under control.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy and letting the bell tip onto the forearm.
exercises.beginnerModification: Just hold the bottoms-up position at shoulder height, or walk with it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The unstable bell forces a strong grip and a straight, stacked pressing path.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
instructions: Bring two bells to the shoulders with the elbows close to the ribs and the wrists firm.
Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart.
Dip a little at the knees and hips, then drive hard through the floor.
Use that drive to punch both arms straight overhead, then pull the elbows down to the rack.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward onto the toes and pressing before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use one bell at a time, or a strict press with lighter bells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Leg drive lets you move more weight overhead than a strict press.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
instructions: Rack two bells at the shoulders with the elbows close to the ribs and the wrists firm.
Dip slightly at the knees and hips with a tall back.
Drive up hard, then split the feet front and back as you punch both arms straight.
Stand up with the feet back under the hips, then pull the elbows down to the rack.
exercises.formCue: Drive up, drop under, lock out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bells out slowly instead of getting under them, and a short unstable split.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the double push press first and practise the footwork with no weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains power and timing by getting the body under a heavy overhead load.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand shoulder width apart and hold the bell in one hand, palm down, with a firm grip.
Keep the back flat and sink into the hips to send the bell back between the legs.
Snap the hips forward to float the bell to about chest height, letting the free arm move with it.
Let the bell fall back between the legs and hinge again.
exercises.formCue: Hips throw it, the arm just guides.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting with the shoulder and letting the trunk twist toward the bell.
exercises.beginnerModification: Own the two-hand swing first, then use a lighter bell.
exercises.whyThisMatters: One hand on the bell adds grip work and makes the trunk resist rotation.

exercises.name: Kettlebell High Windmill
instructions: Stand with the feet wider than the shoulders and press one bell straight overhead.
Keep that arm vertical and your eyes on the bell.
Sink back into the hip under the bell and let the free hand slide down the inside of the opposite leg.
Push the hips forward to stand tall again with the arm still locked.
exercises.formCue: Hip back, eyes on the bell.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending sideways through the spine instead of hinging, and a soft overhead elbow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the low windmill or use no weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder stability overhead while the hips and trunk move underneath.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Low Windmill
instructions: Stand with the feet wider than the shoulders, bell hanging in one hand in front of the thigh.
Reach the other arm straight overhead and look at that hand.
Sink back into the hips and lower the bell down the inside of the leg.
Drive through the legs and push the hips forward to stand.
exercises.formCue: Sit into the hip, top arm stays vertical.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no weight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the windmill hinge with the load held low, where it is easier to control.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
instructions: Clean two bells to the rack in front of the shoulders and set the feet in your squat stance.
Brace and keep the elbows in and the chest tall.
Bend the knees and hips and lower until the thighs are just past parallel.
Drive up to full hip and knee extension.
exercises.commonMistakes: Elbows flaring so the bells pull you forward, and the upper back rounding.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use one bell held as a goblet squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The front-loaded bells train the legs and demand a strong, upright trunk.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Figure Eight
instructions: Stand wider than shoulder width and sit into a squat with a flat back, bell in one hand.
Pass the bell between the legs from front to back into the other hand.
Bring it around the outside of that leg to the front.
Pass it back through to the first hand and keep tracing the eight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and standing up between passes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bell and move slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds grip, coordination and trunk control while the legs hold a squat.

exercises.name: Half Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Lie on your back with the bell pressed above one shoulder, that knee bent and the other leg out at an angle.
Keep your eyes on the bell and roll up onto the opposite elbow, then onto the hand.
Push through the planted foot to lift the hips off the floor.
Pause, then reverse each step back to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Eyes on the bell, arm vertical.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing the steps and letting the overhead arm drift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise with no weight, or balance a shoe on the fist.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the first half of the get-up, where shoulder stability and trunk strength are learned.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pull-Over Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat, holding the bell by the sides of the handle past your head.
With the arms long, pull the bell over until it is above the chest.
Crunch up, lifting the shoulder blades off the floor.
Lower the back down, then return the bell overhead.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down as the bell goes back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back when the bell is overhead.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bell, or do the pull-over without the crunch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the abs and lats together and teaches rib control with the arms overhead.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Single-Arm Overhead Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, core
instructions: Press one bell overhead and lock the arm, feet about shoulder width apart.
Keep your eyes on the bell.
Push the hips back and squat, letting the free arm reach toward the floor as the trunk turns slightly toward the bell side.
Drive through both feet to stand with the arm still locked.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the overhead arm bend or drift forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use no weight, or squat with the bell in the rack.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It tests shoulder stability, hip mobility and trunk control together.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: Kettlebell and a chair or bench
instructions: Stand in a split stance with the bell by the back foot and the free hand on a chair or bench.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the bell.
Pull the elbow up and back, keeping it close to the ribs and the chest still.
Lower the bell under control until the arm is straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbow to the hip, chest still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and yanking the bell with a twist of the trunk.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter bell and a higher support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the back one side at a time and shows up left-right differences.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, lower back, hamstrings
instructions: Stand hip width apart with two bells between the feet.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and soft knees, and grip both handles.
Hold the hinge and pull both elbows back.
Lower the bells with control without standing up.
exercises.formCue: Hold the hinge, row to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back and bouncing the torso to move the weight.
exercises.beginnerModification: Row one bell at a time with a hand on a support.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the upper back while the hips and lower back hold a hinge.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Deadlift
instructions: Stand shoulder width apart with the bell on the floor outside one foot.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, bend the knees and grip the handle.
Push through the feet and stand tall without leaning toward or away from the bell.
Hinge back down the same way and set the bell on the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning to the side as you lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the bell on a low step to shorten the reach.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The one-sided load makes the trunk work to keep you upright while you hinge.

exercises.name: American Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Set up as for a two-hand swing and hike the bell back between the legs.
Drive the hips and legs so their force carries the bell upward.
Let the bell travel all the way overhead with the arms straight and the trunk held rigid.
Guide it back down the same path into the next hinge.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back at the top and pulling with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-height swing until the overhead position is comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer path means more work per rep than the chest-height swing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, upper back
instructions: Squat down to dumbbells beside the ankles, palms facing in, shoulders over the weights and back tight.
Stand by extending the hips and knees, keeping the dumbbells close.
As they pass the knees, finish the leg drive and shrug hard.
Pull the elbows under and catch the dumbbells at the shoulders with the knees slightly bent, then stand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Curling the weights up with the arms and letting them drift away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from the hang with the dumbbells at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains fast hip and leg extension with simple equipment.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of the thighs, knees slightly bent and back straight.
Push the hips back and slide the weights down close to the legs.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the back of the legs and the back is still flat.
Push through the heels and bring the hips forward to stand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower and turning it into a squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the range or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the hamstrings and glutes and grooves a clean hip hinge.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
instructions: Stand in a long split stance with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Lower by bending the front knee and hip, letting the back heel rise.
Stop when the back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the front foot to stand, and finish all reps before switching legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: A stance that is too short and the front knee caving in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no weight and hold a support for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads one leg at a time with a stable base, good for strength and balance.

exercises.name: Renegade Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, core, shoulders, triceps
instructions: Take a push-up position with each hand on a dumbbell under the shoulder and the feet about shoulder width apart.
Press into both dumbbells and keep the body straight.
Row one dumbbell toward the chest with the elbow close to the ribs while the feet press into the floor.
Lower it slowly, then row the other side.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hips rotating open on each row and the lower back sagging.
exercises.beginnerModification: Widen the feet, drop to the knees, or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back and the trunk at once by making you resist rotation.

exercises.name: Man-Maker
exercises.musclesWorked: Chest, back, shoulders, quads, glutes, core
instructions: Start in a high plank gripping two dumbbells, feet hip width or wider, and do one push-up.
Row one dumbbell, then the other, without rocking the hips.
Step or jump the feet up to a squat stance and clean the dumbbells to the shoulders.
Squat, stand and press overhead, then lower the weights to the floor and return to the plank.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting during the rows and losing the back position when picking the weights up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use light dumbbells, step instead of jumping, or drop the push-up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strings a push, a pull, a squat and a press into one demanding conditioning rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with the dumbbells in the hip crease, then lie back and bring them to the chest.
Press them to straight arms and set the feet flat with the knees bent.
Lower slowly until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.formCue: Soft touch on the floor, then press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows onto the floor and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use lighter dumbbells or press one arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you press without a bench, and the floor limits how far the shoulders travel.

exercises.name: Arnold Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with the legs straight out and the torso upright.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with the palms facing you.
Press overhead while turning the palms to face forward, and lock out fully.
Lower under control, turning the palms back toward you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the weights go up and rounding the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a low pad, bend the knees slightly, or use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no back support and no leg drive, the shoulders and trunk do all the work.

exercises.name: Zottman Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and palms facing forward.
Curl the weights up with the palms up and the elbows at your sides.
At the top, turn the palms to face down.
Lower slowly with the palms down, then turn them forward again at the bottom.
exercises.formCue: Palms up to lift, palms down to lower.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the weights and rushing the lowering half.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go lighter, or curl one arm at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the biceps on the way up and the forearms on the way down.
